clue.text: Second drink I have makes me frisky

parts.note: port is a fortified wine, a drink
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone finds a second glass of wine puts them in a playful mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of I'VE is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportive person is playful and lively, a close synonym.

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A cheerful melody to sing along to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' looks like praise for the tune, but in a down clue it turns AIR upwards into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is an operatic solo song, a melody written to be sung.

clue.text: People will mind if you dump your kids here

definitions.text: People will mind if you dump your kids here

parts.words: People will mind if you dump your kids here
parts.note: read as a complaint, 'mind' means object; read straight, it means look after: a place where staff care for children left there

explanation.definitionFit: A day nursery where parents leave small children to be looked after.

clue.text: Takes in with the eyes of a sailor

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, so belonging to a sailor is AB'S
orbs is a poetic word for eyes

explanation.surface: Someone looks things over with a seaman's keen gaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the eyes of a sailor' becomes AB'S ORBS, the sailor's eyes, in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb is to soak up or take something into oneself, the same idea.

clue.text: Handy thing to take up or run

definitions.meaning: a protective glove, a thing for the hand
one takes up the challenge glove, and one runs the double line of attackers

explanation.definitionFit: It is a heavy glove, and figures in the idioms 'take up the gauntlet' and 'run the gauntlet'.

parts.note: safety means security
a belt is a zone or band, as in a commuter belt

explanation.surface: A protected area set aside for drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The strap that keeps a driver secure in the seat in a crash.

definitions.meaning: a duplicate made with inked sheets
the inked sheet used to make such duplicates

explanation.definitionFit: Short for both a carbon copy and carbon paper.

definitions.meaning: a cut of pork from the ribs
in Genesis Eve was made from one of Adam's ribs, one he could spare

explanation.definitionFit: A cut of pork ribs, and literally the rib Adam could spare to create Eve.

clue.text: Mount framing an artist in his element

indicators.note: framing means one piece goes round another like a picture frame

parts.note: art is the artist's element, the world he works in
an gives A
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A picture mount around a painter who feels completely at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like the picture mount suggested by 'framing'; it is the mountain. 'his element' refers back to the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ararat is the mountain in Turkey on which Noah's ark came to rest.

clue.text: Sailing vessel with a professional second mate

parts.note: pro is short for professional

indicators.note: second picks the second letter of the word mate

explanation.surface: A boat crewed by a paid expert and a second-in-command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second mate' looks like a ship's officer, apt for a vessel, but 'second' just picks the second letter of 'mate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A proa is a Malay outrigger sailing boat.

parts.note: the Crown stands for the sovereign
the Derby is a famous English horse race run at Epsom

explanation.surface: A remark about which horse race the Chinese monarch favours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is porcelain; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown Derby is a brand of fine porcelain made in Derby, England.

clue.text: Little time to note what happened?

definitions.meaning: a very short period of time, sixty seconds
to record the proceedings of a meeting in writing

explanation.definitionFit: A brief moment, and as a verb to record the official record of a meeting.

definitions.meaning: the realm of the dead in mythology, Hades
organised crime and its members as a whole

explanation.definitionFit: Both the mythological realm of the dead and the world of organised crime.

clue.text: Two students put inside, paying for playground tyranny

indicators.note: put inside means the students' letters are placed within another word

parts.note: buying means paying for something
L, a learner, stands for a student, so two give LL

explanation.surface: Two pupils are locked away for paying to bully others at school.
explanation.walkthrough: L is a learner driver's plate, so a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullying is intimidation of the weak, the sort of tyranny found in school playgrounds.

parts.note: read as 'no snag', it really means no fish can be caught in this water, too salty for life

explanation.definitionFit: The salt lake between Israel and Jordan, too saline for fish.

clue.text: Feelings shown by people put Into some distress

indicators.note: distress means the letters are put into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: People in some trouble show how they feel.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of INTO and SOME are rearranged; 'shown by people put' is surface padding linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotions are feelings such as joy or anger, a synonym.

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters are handled in a crafty way and rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Streams are flows of water, currents.

indicators.note: somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tries to squeeze names onto a register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' tempts a container reading, but here it is only a link and 'Somehow' governs both words together.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifest is a list of cargo or passengers.

clue.text: Formed a queue at the back

definitions.text: Formed a queue at the back

parts.words: Formed a queue at the back
parts.note: a queue is also a pigtail hanging at the back of the head; forming one means braiding the hair

explanation.definitionFit: Braided hair into a pigtail, which hangs at the back of the head.

parts.note: a daily is a char, a cleaning woman who comes in each day
coal is a fuel

explanation.surface: A newspaper supplies fuel for the fire every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like an adverb or a newspaper; in British usage a daily is a charwoman, a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Charcoal sticks are used by artists to sketch.

clue.text: It carries food for a flea, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a container that feeds grain or feed into a machine or trough
a flea is a jumping insect, an example of something that hops

explanation.definitionFit: A funnel-shaped feed container, and anything that hops, like a flea.

indicators.note: inside means the metal is placed within the scrap

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Sorting scrap metal by quality in a yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating is a grade or classification.

clue.text: Haphazard arrangement of right and order

parts.note: and is taken as written
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Things placed any old way, neither tidy nor correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement of' is a link here, not an anagram signal; the pieces go in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Random means by chance, without plan, like haphazard.

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
a position is a place

explanation.surface: A complaint that a job is not in the civil service.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament the opposition is the party or parties not in power.

clue.text: Carefully analyse Kipling's work, in a way

indicators.note: in means the poem is placed inside the way

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
'If' is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem

explanation.surface: A literature student studies a Kipling poem closely, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' reads like a hedging phrase, but 'in' is the container signal; Kipling's best-known poem is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To sift evidence is to examine it closely, as through a sieve.

definitions.meaning: to dismiss someone from a job
Shakespeare's Falstaff loved ..., a dry white wine from Spain

explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss someone, and the old Spanish wine Falstaff drank.

definitions.meaning: Irving ..., the American composer of White Christmas

explanation.definitionFit: Germany's capital, and Irving Berlin the American composer.

parts.note: sounds like prohibition of alcohol, but means driving out evil spirits from a person or place

explanation.definitionFit: Ritual expulsion of demons or ghosts.
